slides.2.title: The Geography and Terroir of the Médoc Peninsula
slides.2.content:
🗺️ Core Knowledge Points

Location
  • A narrow peninsula on the Left Bank of the Gironde estuary
  • Extends approximately 60 km north-west of the city of Bordeaux towards the Atlantic
  • About 15 km wide; total area approximately 16,500 hectares
Soil Characteristics
  • Predominantly gravel soils (Graves)
  • Exceptional drainage and heat retention
  • Ideally suited to Cabernet Sauvignon
Climatic Advantages
  • Dual moderation from the Atlantic and the Gironde
  • Mild maritime climate
  • The river provides frost protection
slides.2.quiz.question: For which grape variety are the gravel soils of the Médoc peninsula best suited?
slides.2.quiz.explanation: The Médoc's gravel soils provide excellent drainage and heat retention — ideal conditions for the late-ripening Cabernet Sauvignon to reach full maturity and develop its powerful structure and complex flavours.
slides.3.title: Comparing the Four Star Appellations of the Médoc
slides.3.description: A deep understanding of the differences between Margaux, Pauillac, Saint-Julien, and Saint-Estèphe
slides.3.quiz.question: Which appellation is considered the most "balanced" in the Médoc, combining elegance with power?
slides.3.quiz.explanation: Saint-Julien is celebrated as the most balanced appellation in the Médoc. Its soil composition (an ideal ratio of gravel to clay) and varietal blends mean its wines combine the elegance of Margaux with the power of Pauillac.

slides.6.title: Pomerol: The Secret of a Rare Gem
slides.6.content:
💎 The Uniqueness of Pomerol

🗺️ Geographic Scale

Bordeaux's smallest major appellation — just approximately 800 hectares

On the Right Bank of the Dordogne, immediately adjacent to Saint-Émilion

🪨 Distinctive Soils

Blue Clay — the soul of Pomerol

Rich in iron; high water retention; ideal for Merlot

Gravel on the plateau adds drainage and complexity

👑 No Official Classification

No formal classification system — reputation rests on quality alone

Pétrus — recognised as the "uncrowned king"

Other top estates: Le Pin, Lafleur, Vieux Château Certan

🍇 Merlot-Dominant

Merlot accounts for 80–100% of plantings

Style: full, velvety, intensely fruity

Aromas: black plum, truffle, black cherry, chocolate
slides.6.quiz.question: For which variety is Pomerol's Blue Clay most suited?
slides.6.quiz.explanation: Pomerol's Blue Clay is rich in iron and retains moisture well — providing ideal growing conditions for Merlot and enabling it to develop concentrated fruit flavours and a velvety texture.
slides.7.title: Saint-Émilion: The Greatest Jewel of the Right Bank
slides.7.content:
🏰 Saint-Émilion in Full

📍 Geography and Scale
  • The Right Bank's largest appellation — approximately 5,400 hectares
  • On the Right Bank of the Dordogne; rich in topographic variation
  • A medieval market town; a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Site
🗺️ Soils and Terrain Zones
  • Plateau (Côtes): Limestone soils; Cabernet Franc excels
  • Hillside (Piedmont): Mixed sandy and clay soils; diverse styles
  • Plain (Graves): Gravel soils; style akin to the Left Bank
🏅 Saint-Émilion Classification
  • Premier Grand Cru Classé A: Highest tier (4 châteaux)
    • Château Ausone (plateau limestone)
    • Château Cheval Blanc (gravel plain)
    • Château Angélus
    • Château Pavie
  • Premier Grand Cru Classé B: 14 top châteaux
  • Grand Cru Classé: 64 quality estates
  • Re-evaluated every 10 years (unlike the permanent 1855 Left Bank classification)
🍇 Varietal Profile
  • Merlot: Dominant variety (~60%), contributing generous fruit
  • Cabernet Franc: Important supporting role (~30%), adding elegance and aromatic complexity
  • Style sits between the power of the Left Bank and the suppleness of Pomerol
slides.7.quiz.question: What is the most important difference between Saint-Émilion's classification and the 1855 Left Bank classification?
slides.7.quiz.explanation: Saint-Émilion's classification is re-evaluated every 10 years to ensure rankings reflect current quality — a sharp contrast to the 1855 classification, which has remained essentially unchanged. This reflects a more dynamic approach to quality management.
slides.8.title: Pomerol vs Saint-Émilion: A Tale of Two Right Bank Stars
slides.8.description: Understanding the similarities and differences between the two great Right Bank appellations
slides.8.quiz.question: Why are Pomerol wines typically priced extremely high?
slides.8.quiz.options.1: Because the appellation is small and production is scarce
slides.8.quiz.options.3: Because it has the oldest classification
slides.8.quiz.explanation: Pomerol is Bordeaux's smallest major appellation — just approximately 800 hectares — with extremely limited production. Combined with the world-class quality of top estates such as Pétrus, scarcity and outstanding quality together drive prices to extraordinary levels.

slides.11.content:
📋 Assessment Objectives

This comprehensive assessment will test your command of the Level 2 content, including:

  • ✅ Terroir characteristics of the four star Left Bank appellations
  • ✅ Differences between Pomerol and Saint-Émilion on the Right Bank
  • ✅ The relationship between appellation soils and grape varieties
  • ✅ Understanding and application of classification systems
  • ✅ Ability to identify representative châteaux
🎯 Passing Standard

Answer 12 or more questions correctly (80%) to pass the assessment and qualify to advance to Level 3.

Level 3 will take you deeper into the science of Bordeaux terroir, climate change, winemaking craft, and other advanced topics.

slides.12.componentProps.items.0.questio: What was the primary geological process that formed the gravelly soils of the Médoc peninsula?
slides.12.componentProps.items.0.explana: Médoc's gravelly soils mainly originate from Quaternary glacial-period river alluviation — sediment carried by the Garonne and Dordogne deposited deep gravel layers at the Gironde estuary.
slides.12.componentProps.items.1.questio: Which appellation is renowned for an "elegant, silk-smooth" wine style?
slides.12.componentProps.items.1.explana: Margaux is famous for its elegant, silky style — dubbed the "perfume of Médoc". Its fine gravelly soils produce this distinctive elegance.
slides.12.componentProps.items.2.questio: How many 1855 First Growths (Premiers Crus) does Pauillac appellation have?
slides.12.componentProps.items.2.explana: Pauillac has 3 First Growths: Château Lafite Rothschild, Château Latour, and Château Mouton Rothschild (promoted in 1973) — the most of any single appellation.
slides.12.componentProps.items.3.questio: What is the defining characteristic of the Saint-Julien appellation?
slides.12.componentProps.items.3.explana: Saint-Julien is regarded as the most balanced Médoc appellation. Its ideal gravel-clay soil mix and variety blend create a perfect harmony of elegance and power.
slides.12.componentProps.items.4.questio: Why does Saint-Estèphe have a higher proportion of Merlot than other Médoc village appellations?
slides.12.componentProps.items.4.options: Higher clay content in the soil
slides.12.componentProps.items.4.explana: Saint-Estèphe has higher clay content, giving better water retention and suiting the earlier-ripening Merlot. A higher Merlot proportion also helps soften the appellation's characteristically firm tannins.
slides.12.componentProps.items.5.questio: What is the most famous soil type in the Pomerol appellation?
slides.12.componentProps.items.5.explana: Pomerol's most celebrated soil is its Blue Clay, rich in iron with excellent water retention, providing ideal growing conditions for Merlot. It is the terroir foundation of estates like Pétrus.
slides.12.componentProps.items.6.questio: What is the approximate vineyard area of Château Pétrus?
slides.12.componentProps.items.6.explana: Château Pétrus has only ~11.5 hectares. Its tiny production (~30,000 bottles/year) combined with exceptional quality makes it one of the world's most expensive wines.
slides.12.componentProps.items.7.questio: What is distinctive about the Saint-Émilion classification system?
slides.12.componentProps.items.7.explana: The Saint-Émilion classification is reassessed roughly every 10 years (most recently in 2022), ensuring it reflects current quality — in contrast to the fixed 1855 Médoc classification.
slides.12.componentProps.items.8.questio: In the current classification, how many châteaux hold Saint-Émilion Premier Grand Cru Classé A status?
slides.12.componentProps.items.8.explana: In the 2022 classification, four châteaux hold Premier Grand Cru Classé A status: Ausone, Cheval Blanc, Angélus, and Pavie.
slides.12.componentProps.items.9.questio: In which topographic zone of Saint-Émilion is Château Ausone located?
slides.12.componentProps.items.9.explana: Château Ausone is on Saint-Émilion's limestone côtes (plateau), where steep south-facing slopes and limestone soils give the wine elegant minerality and excellent ageing potential.
slides.12.componentProps.items.10.questi: In which topographic zone of Saint-Émilion is Château Cheval Blanc located?
slides.12.componentProps.items.10.explan: Château Cheval Blanc is in the north-western gravel plain (Graves) of Saint-Émilion, adjoining Pomerol. Its soil resembles the Left Bank, producing a uniquely styled wine.
slides.12.componentProps.items.11.questi: Which appellation typically has the highest proportion of Cabernet Franc plantings?
slides.12.componentProps.items.11.explan: Saint-Émilion's limestone Côtes are ideal for Cabernet Franc, which can make up 30–40% of the blend here — higher than on the Left Bank or in Pomerol — adding elegant floral notes and minerality.
slides.12.componentProps.items.12.questi: Where did the Bordeaux "Vin de Garage" (Garage Wine) movement originate?
slides.12.componentProps.items.12.explan: The Garage Wine movement originated in the 1990s in the Libournais (especially Saint-Émilion satellites), challenging tradition with tiny volumes and extreme quality. Key estates: Le Pin, Valandraud.
slides.12.componentProps.items.13.questi: What is the main philosophical difference between Left Bank and Right Bank winemaking?
slides.12.componentProps.items.13.option: Left Bank more traditional; Right Bank more innovative
Left Bank emphasises structure and ageing; Right Bank emphasises fruit and approachability
Left Bank exclusively uses new oak; Right Bank uses none
Left Bank has larger volumes; Right Bank smaller
slides.12.componentProps.items.13.explan: Left Bank (especially classed growths) traditionally emphasises Cabernet Sauvignon structure, tannins, and long-term ageing; Right Bank focuses more on Merlot's fruit expression and youthful approachability.
slides.12.componentProps.items.14.questi: Which of the following statements is correct?
slides.12.componentProps.items.14.option: Pomerol has an official classification system
The 1855 Médoc classification can be revised every 10 years
Pomerol has no official classification but Pétrus is universally acknowledged as the top estate
slides.12.componentProps.items.14.explan: Pomerol is the only major Bordeaux appellation without an official classification, but Château Pétrus is universally recognised as the region's "uncrowned king", with prices matching or exceeding First Growths.
slides.12.componentProps.items.15.questi: What major event was behind the establishment of the 1855 Classification?
slides.12.componentProps.items.15.option: End of the Franco-Prussian War celebrations
slides.12.componentProps.items.15.explan: To mark the 1855 Paris World Exhibition, Napoleon III requested the Bordeaux Chamber of Commerce create a classification to showcase France's finest wines to the world.
slides.12.componentProps.items.16.questi: What is the most geographically distinctive feature of Pauillac compared to other Médoc village appellations?
slides.12.componentProps.items.16.option: Closest to the Atlantic, most directly ocean-influenced
Borders the Gironde estuary, with the best-draining gravel ridges
Highest clay proportion, best water retention
slides.12.componentProps.items.16.explan: Pauillac borders the Gironde estuary and has the most typical deep gravel ridges (plateaux de graves) in the Médoc, providing excellent drainage and producing structured, long-lived Cabernet Sauvignon.
slides.12.componentProps.items.17.questi: What is the name of Château Margaux's Second Wine?
slides.12.componentProps.items.17.explan: "Pavillon Rouge du Château Margaux" is noted for elegance and is considered one of the finest Second Wines, reflecting the grand vin's character.
slides.12.componentProps.items.18.questi: What is the role of the Landes pine forest to the west of Médoc in viticulture?
slides.12.componentProps.items.18.option: Blocks Atlantic gales and moderates Médoc's climate
slides.12.componentProps.items.18.explan: The Landes, Europe's largest planted forest, lies to the west of Médoc and acts as a natural barrier against Atlantic gales and excessive rainfall — a key factor in Médoc's mild oceanic climate.
slides.12.componentProps.items.19.questi: Which is the only estate from Graves included in the 1855 Médoc First Growth classification?
slides.12.componentProps.items.19.explan: Château Haut-Brion is the only non-Médoc estate in the 1855 Classification, included as a First Growth. Its history dates back to the 17th century.
slides.12.componentProps.items.20.questi: Why is the soil on the Pomerol plateau particularly precious?
slides.12.componentProps.items.20.option: The top layer contains iron-rich clay marl (crasse de fer) and blue clay
slides.12.componentProps.items.20.explan: The iron-rich clay marl (crasse de fer) and blue clay at the top of the Pomerol plateau have outstanding water retention, forming the terroir advantage of estates like Pétrus and Le Pin.
slides.12.componentProps.items.21.questi: In the 1855 Classification, which tier has the most estates?
slides.12.componentProps.items.21.explan: The Fifth Growth (Cinquième Cru) has 18 estates — the most of any tier — mainly in Pauillac and Saint-Estèphe.
slides.12.componentProps.items.22.questi: What is the key role of the Ciron River in the production of Sauternes sweet wine?
slides.12.componentProps.items.22.option: Creates morning mist that promotes Botrytis cinerea development
Supplies mineral nutrients to the soil
slides.12.componentProps.items.22.explan: The cold Ciron River creates morning mist when it meets the warmer Garonne, promoting noble rot; afternoon sunshine disperses the mist and prevents grey rot — a microclimate unique to Sauternes.
slides.12.componentProps.items.23.questi: Which of the following is a satellite appellation of Saint-Émilion?
slides.12.componentProps.items.23.explan: Lussac-Saint-Émilion is a satellite appellation to the north of Saint-Émilion, permitted to include "Saint-Émilion" in its name. Merlot-dominant, similar in style but more accessible in price.
slides.12.componentProps.items.24.questi: What does the Médoc's "Crus Bourgeois" system represent?
slides.12.componentProps.items.24.option: An extension of the 1855 classified growths
A quality certification for non-classified estates (in three tiers)
A special designation for the most expensive Médoc wines
slides.12.componentProps.items.24.explan: Crus Bourgeois is a quality certification for Médoc non-classified estates. The 2020 revision introduced three tiers: Cru Bourgeois, Cru Bourgeois Supérieur, and Cru Bourgeois Exceptionnel.
slides.12.componentProps.items.25.questi: What is the relationship between Haut-Médoc AOC and the village appellations within it?
slides.12.componentProps.items.25.option: Haut-Médoc is the broader AOC encompassing the six village appellations
Haut-Médoc quality exceeds all village appellations
slides.12.componentProps.items.25.explan: Haut-Médoc AOC covers the high-quality southern Médoc, containing six key village appellations (Margaux, Moulis, Listrac, Saint-Julien, Pauillac, Saint-Estèphe). Village appellations are subsets of Haut-Médoc.
slides.12.componentProps.items.26.questi: What is the geographic role of the Dordogne River in the Bordeaux appellation landscape?
slides.12.componentProps.items.26.option: Forms the main Right Bank river, nurturing Saint-Émilion and Pomerol
Separates the two sides of Médoc
Carries alluvial deposits to form the Left Bank gravels
slides.12.componentProps.items.26.explan: The Dordogne flows westward to join the Gironde estuary; its right bank nurtures Saint-Émilion, Pomerol, Fronsac and other key Right Bank appellations.
slides.12.componentProps.items.27.questi: Compared to other Médoc villages, what is the most distinctive soil characteristic of Margaux AOC?
slides.12.componentProps.items.27.option: Finest gravel, least clay, producing the most refined style
Highest clay proportion, best water retention
slides.12.componentProps.items.27.explan: Margaux's gravel is finer, soils more impoverished, clay layer shallowest — creating lower natural yields, more concentrated aromatics, and elegant tannin structure.
slides.12.componentProps.items.28.questi: Saint-Julien AOC has no First Growth, but its classified estates as a whole are noted for what?
slides.12.componentProps.items.28.option: Highest average quality and most consistent classified estates
Only village appellation with no classified estates
slides.12.componentProps.items.28.explan: Saint-Julien has 5 Second Growths (Léoville Las Cases, Léoville Barton, Léoville Poyferré, Ducru-Beaucaillou, Gruaud-Larose), consistently high-quality — earning it the title of "most reliable Médoc village".
slides.12.componentProps.items.29.questi: What are the legal requirements for using the term "Château" on a Bordeaux wine label?
slides.12.componentProps.items.29.option: Must have a medieval castle building
Must own its own vineyards and make wine on the same estate
slides.12.componentProps.items.29.explan: In Bordeaux, "Château" broadly refers to an estate winery with its own vineyards making wine on the premises — no actual castle building is required. Used by estates of all sizes.
slides.4.takeaways.0.detail: From Margaux fine gravel to Saint-Estephe clay, soil composition directly shapes the balance between power and elegance.
slides.4.takeaways.1.detail: The Left Bank gravelly soils and oceanic climate provide ideal conditions for the late-ripening Cabernet Sauvignon.
slides.4.takeaways.2.detail: Of 61 classified estates, 60 are from Medoc (1 from Graves), cementing the Left Bank s status on the world wine stage.
slides.9.takeaways.0.detail: The clay soils of the Right Bank provide the ideal environment for Merlot, creating a smooth, fruit-forward style distinctly different from the Left Bank.
slides.9.takeaways.1.detail: From Pomerol blue clay to Saint-Emilion limestone plateau, soil diversity generates a rich range of wine styles.
slides.9.takeaways.2.detail: Pomerol has no official classification yet its top estates are world-renowned; Saint-Emilion s dynamic classification ensures quality continuously improves.
